Phainon had just been tasked with the most arduous mission he’s been asked to execute by far.

The maiden of passage, Tribios, and the Goldweaver, Aglaea, stand poised in front of him. Aglaea’s face is stern but composed, and there’s a hint of worry in Tribios’ usually warm eyes.

“Phainon,” Aglaea starts. “Time is of the essence. As the Deliverer, you are about to be sent on your most arduous mission yet.” Tribios nodded in agreement beside her.

“We must put an end to this overwhelming strife. You will have to face the crown prince of strife and bring us victory.” She pauses before continuing, her gaze apologetic. “Otherwise, Okhema will face great calamity and will be overtaken by strife.” Her expression is devoid of her usual optimism.

Phainon sighs upon hearing his task. He had almost expected this much. Lately, titankin of strife have been more ferocious than ever, invading the holy kingdom frequently, and they’ve especially had an eye out for Phainon’s head. Luckily, the heirs have managed to prevent many casualties, thanks to their most skilled healer, Hyacine. Blessed by Aquila, Hyacine’s healing magic is the best of all in Amphoreus. Phainon would not be able to fight as efficiently as he’s able to, if not for her aid.

Though a heavy burden, Phainon isn’t afraid in the slightest to do what needs to be done for Okhema, and all of Amphoreus. He’s seen how much the frequent strife has frightened the civilians and taken a toll onto the heirs, and he’s glad to take the weight off their backs.

“I will shoulder this responsibility,” Phainon said, voice steady and unshaken. It’s about time someone confronts the demon prince of strife, with how his titankin have been terrorizing all of their kingdom.

But there’s one thing… The crown prince is widely feared for his immortality. Those who have seen him face to face don’t live to tell the story, disposed of quicker than one could blink. To the prince, claiming the lives of mortals is like stepping on a measly insect, inferior and irrelevant. He could only pity their futile struggle.

“Courageous as ever, Phainon,” Aglaea said, softly. “Okhema is indebted to you.”

“The first step of the journey is to get in touch with the Mage of Death in Aidonia, Castorice. Her knowledge of the divine exceeds all in Amphoreus.” Tribios summons a map with the sleight of her hand.

“Traverse through the land that reveres death and seek her power. As the acolyte of Thanatos, only she is capable of guiding us towards victory.”

And so, Phainon sets off to Aidonia, the frozen land. Carrying his most trustworthy companion, Dawnmaker, he makes quick work of any titankin or black tide creatures that attempt to block his path. Though the cold of the never-ceasing snow bites at his skin, he perseveres.

It’s a good thing that he remembers the alchemy lessons from his academy days, taught by Professor Anaxagoras. Phainon was never a prodigy when it came to alchemy and incantations, hence why he’s more suited to wield a sword. He gulps down the warmth potion, and the cold sting of freezing air fades away quickly.

Aidonia has a unique way of welcoming those who tread upon their land. He’s had countless people approach him, preaching about ‘giving into death.’ He has no plans of receiving the ‘blessing’ of death anytime soon, so he must politely decline and push through.

Though his legs and shoulders ache slightly, at least he is accompanied by the beautiful aurora washing over Aidonia’s dark sky. Ribbons and sweeping arcs of turquoise and deep aqua light dance in the sky, almost as if they are moving in tandem with the twinkling stars.

By the time the sun is rising once more, he’s nearing his location, according to the map given to him by Tribios. But he doesn’t spot any tall, magnificent tower that seems like it would belong to a great mage. There’s only a secluded cabin atop the snowy hill in front of him. Approaching with caution, he hikes up the slope, the sound of crushing fresh snow under his feet pleasant to his ears.

He knocks once, twice, awaiting an answer. A beat of anticipatory silence passes before the door slowly creaks open, purple eyes peeking through the small crack, flickering with alert. Another awkward moment, and the door fully swings open. Phainon is greeted by the frail figure of the mage, who wears a white dress that burns at the edges with the trace of death, and a dark shawl draped over her shoulders. “Greetings, Lord Phainon,” she nods, formal as ever.

“It’s so nice to see you again, Cas!” Phainon grins, radiating warmth.

“You may come in, but just as always, keep five paces distance, lest you be tainted by the misfortune of death.” Phainon follows her inside of the cabin, pulling the snow-covered hood of his cloak down. The inside of her cabin is warm and comforting; Phainon immediately feels more at ease as he settles down. “Make yourself comfortable,” Castorice adds, directing her gaze to the couch accompanied by the warmth of her fireplace. “Allow me to pour you a cup of tea. It’s not often that I see my fellow graduates,” she smiles.

The cabin smells of lavender and all sorts of floral, woody herbs. Across her kitchen counter, countless flowers and unique plants are scattered, twinkling with a twinge of enchantment. Phainon exhales with relief as he sits himself onto the comfy cushion. Castorice approaches him from behind not long after, setting a tray of teacups and sugar cubes onto the table, before sitting down across from him.

“Thank you, Cas.” Phainon took in the soothing scent of his tea before taking a sip, the floral and mellow sweetness of the tea setting on his tongue.

“Of course. It’s chamomile, made for relaxation, and I added some honey ambrosia to sweeten it,” she clarified, raising the teacup to her lips. “Now then, let's get to the task at hand. I’ve been expecting you, as Lady Aglaea kept me up to date.”

“Yes, I’ve been tasked with the duty of defeating the prince of strife. If I do not bring us victory, the prophecy tells that Okhema will face a great calamity,” Phainon explained. Castorice’s brow furrowed upon understanding that this was not a light matter.

“As far as we know, he has one weakness that will bypass his immortality, but we’ve yet to decipher what it is.”

Castorice’s eyes sharpen, silence overtaking them as Phainon allows her to think.

“It’s true,” she says dryly. Phainon’s ears perk up. “I am most suited for this task, because I am an acolyte of Thanatos. Though unfortunately, casting a spell this strong will drain a lot of mana… But I’m willing to do what it takes.”

Phainon nods with appreciation, “Thank you, Castorice. This couldn’t be done without you. When I return from my victory, I’ll be sure to give you the highest of honors.” Castorice’s head tilted as she smiled warmly. “Come now, Lord Phainon.”

Castorice stands up, taking her staff along with her. Phainon quickly follows suite, trailing behind her as she steps out of the back door.

The scenery in front of him seems empty, a vast land of nothing but snow, until Castorice whispers under her breath and taps her staff to the ground. In a flash, incoherent whispers of titan's echo throughout his head, and when he blinks his eyes open, the view has changed. What was once a barren plot of frost has now turned into a flourishing garden, blooming across the snow. Purple wisteria trees and numerous flowers crowd over a pathway that leads to an incantation circle. “This is an amazing garden you have,” Phainon said.

Castorice’s expression is full of warmth upon receiving his praise. “This is where I cast particularly stronger spells, or communicate with the Titans.” In this case, she’ll be doing both. She treads down the path, petals flowing throughout the air, with Phainon following, peering around the garden. They come to a halt at the border of the magic circle, which is glowing and twinkling with energy, glowing from pure-white snow.

“Allow me, and please be cautious. This may take a moment,” she warns, kneeling in the middle of the circle, staff propped on her lap. Phainon steps back as she starts to whisper to herself once again, in the language of the Titans, holding her clasped hands to her chest.

The next moment, the incarnation circle is glowing brighter than before; the energy gradually growing taller as if it were walls that encased Castorice inside. Through the beaming light, he can see Castorice’s staff trembling with mana as it conjures power from the River of Souls, the searing coreflame of death glowing profusely. Just as quickly, another searing flash of light obscures his vision. He flinches, and steps back before he can open his eyes again.

Crystalized, translucent shards start to build up from ice. They eventually take the figure of a tall, muscular and — Utterly beautiful man.

The ancient illustrations of the prince don’t compare to a fraction of the beauty he sees right now.

His — very well defined — upper body is clad in a black coat that frames his middle perfectly. His shoulder-length, strawberry blonde hair seems to flow even in the frozen air of time. Curved black horns protrude from the upper sides of his head.

…He almost can't take his eyes away from the red ink lines that frame his defined and plump chest.

No, no! This is your enemy, you can’t let yourself be drawn in by his conspicuous body. He shakes his head, snapping out of his trance.

“Castorice,” he instinctively reaches out, though drawing back once he remembers that he must keep his distance. “Are you alright?”

She exhales sharply before nodding. “I’m okay,” she sighed with a shaky breath, turning to face him. “That just took quite a bit out of me.”

Phainon nodded in understanding. His eyes drift onto the crystalline figures of memories. “What exactly are these?”

“These are echoes of the past, extracted from the River of Souls. Here is Prince Mydeimos crawling out of death’s clutches again and again.” She rises from her knees, using her staff to prop her up.

“Death is whispering to me.” Castorice’s hand ghosts right through the figure upon touching it, and there's an intense light radiating from that particular spot high on his back.

“His only weak point is precisely… his tenth thoracic vertebrae. This is the only way to defeat him.”

Such a specific weakness, not a soul would be able to figure it out without calling upon the knowledge of the divine. “So, this is what a great mage is capable of?”

“There is no need to gawk, Lord Phainon,” Castorice chuckles half-heartedly. “I am simply able to do this because I bear the curse of death.” Castorice’s smile strains slightly, though she tries to keep a soft expression on her face. There’s a barely audible ache in her tone.

“It’s not just a curse,” Phainon said. “We wouldn’t have guidance without your power.”

Castorice goes quiet for a moment, before looking up from the ground. “I suppose thats true. Thank you, Lord Phainon,” she said. “You should be off now. You have a difficult trial that awaits you.” Her kind and tired eyes soften.

“Of course, Castorice. I am in your debt. Please take care of yourself until you’ve recovered your energy.” She nods in response to that.

With his newfound knowledge, Phainon sets off once again, towards the abandoned kingdom of strife.


He navigates through the densely packed woods, rays of moonlight peeking through the gaps of the leaves. Phainon follows along the trail, enlightened by the glow of the creation nymphs that rest on the bark of the trees. The sound of the breeze sifting through the leaves feels like the trees are whispering among him.

Through the corner of his eye, he can’t help but notice a certain nymph that rests upon a tree stump. It glows a deep indigo, and for some reason, he feels a force that compels him to approach it. He offers his hand towards the nymph, and cautiously, it crawls into his palm.

Abruptly, a flash of light rips through his vision. He jolts, almost stumbling backwards like a clumsy fool. The sound of high-pitched laughter fills the air, and in the next moment, confetti…? falls over him.

“Well, well, if it isn’t the magnificent Deliverer!” The now revealed spiritheif chirps.

“Bartholos?” Phainon utters in confusion. “What are you doing here?”

“I heard through the grapevine that you’re off to Castrum Kremnos, and— “

A blurred line of lightning passes between them. An unknown force twirls him around, causing him to stumble again. And within the next second, a girl appears at the side of Bartholos, her feline tail swinging behind her. A unique looking coin spins in the air before she clutches it in her palm.

She sniffs the air around him cautiously, trying to pick up a specific scent. The scent of death.

Though dizzy, he steadies himself on his feet. Any more sudden movements or surprises and he might hurl honestly.

“And I’ve come to aid you!” Cipher, the fleet footed traveler, chimes in enthusiastically.

“Oh, Cipher! You’ll… aid me?” Phainon said. She nods with a smile plastered across her face.

“Yup!” She enunciates the p with a ‘pop.’ “In exchange that you do a very, very small favor for me.”

“I don’t really know if I can trust that this ‘favor’ you ask of me is small.” Phainon tilts his head, smiling awkwardly. There’s no bad blood between the two, but this is Cipher he’s talking about.

“Psh, cmon, Deliverer boy! I’m telling the truth.” She brings two hands to her chest in a sincere motion, acting as if her feelings have been deeply hurt. “Don’t believe me? Here’s the deal.” She eyes at Bartholos, sticking her hand out to them. They then create a small portal between their hands.

An unknown root of some sort falls right into Cipher’s hand. The herb glows and glitters as if trying to tempt him.

“This right here, is the tradeoff. Digest this magic little plant, and you’ll gain just enough strength to pass the lengthy trial of strife, guaranteed.”

Phainon’s ears perk up. Cipher offers the plant to him, and he takes it into his hand, inspecting it cautiously. “How can I be sure you’re not pulling one over on me?”

Her tail stops swinging before she speaks, frozen in place. “Because Aglaea would cut my tail off and stuff it in my mouth if I were to get in the way of your task.” Her tone is cold and serious, concerningly devoid of her usual playfulness. Well, that’s enough proof that she’s telling the truth.

“…And what do I need to do for you?” Phainon scratches the back of his head.

“Fill me in on the whereabouts of the great mage Lady Castorice!”

That was unexpected. Why did she need that? “Why do you want her whereabouts?”

“Because… On a fleeting evening, we crossed paths, and her beauty caught my eye. Before I could ask where she's from, she left abruptly, claiming there were urgent matters she had to attend to.” She dramatically brings the back of her hand to her forehead, imitating the image of a distressed maiden.

“Why not ask Aglaea?”

“Titans, you ask too many questions,” she sighs. “She’d only tell me if it were an urgent matter, with how high of status Castorice is. And to her, me trying to bag a baddie isn’t an urgent matter!”

Ah, he gets it now.

“Alright, deal! Easy as pie!” He summons the map given to him by Aglaea. “You can take this, I have no need anymore.” Cipher’s eyes light up.

“Eat up, Deliverer boy!”

Suddenly, faster than sight or sound can process, the magic plant has disappeared from the palm of his hand and into his mouth. He nearly chokes.

The plant tastes like… A plant. Freshly pulled from the ground. Dirt. And it scratches the inside of his throat when he swallows. “Titans—” he coughs and sputters, his mouth feeling dry and itchy. “You don’t have, like, water or something?”

“No need! Give it a second,” she sneers.

Give it a second he did. And suddenly, he feels a force of energy rush through his veins, an unknown sense of strength invading his body. He blinks profusely, palms raising in surprise. “This is…?”

“You can thank me later! I’ve gotta dash now,” she sang. Faster than he could say something, she disappears with the wind.

Well, this certainly makes things a little easier, he hopes.
